transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-26
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Alvarez (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO, Praxis AI), Elena Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Samir Khan (Infra), Maya (PM)

Summary section (auto): Jenna - Quick recap: goal is to pick model(s) and deployment for Praxis productization — long context, multilingual, needs tool-calling for retrieval + database ops, concerned about cost and compliance.

[00:00] Jenna: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros — I'm Jenna AE on Redwood, with Marcus our SE. Go ahead and introduce please.
[00:18] Ravi: Hey this is Ravi, CTO at Praxis. We're evaluating options for inference — leaning towards open models and need advice on hosted vs dedicated.
[00:25] Elena: Hi Elena here, lead ML, I'll own model eval; need good Spanish + French answers, and tool-calling to hit our internal DB and vector search.
[00:34] Samir: Samir, infra — network constraints, we may need VPC or private in future.
[00:40] Marcus: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: collect requirements, talk model tradeoffs (LLaMA/Llama3, Mistral, community quantized variants), context length, tool-calling, then narrow deployment recs.
[00:55] Jenna: Also we'll share a deck and security pack after the call — link goes out.
[01:02] Ravi: Perfect. First reqs: we want 32k context baseline, potentially 64k for long-doc summarization. Latency target is sub-600ms for short prompts, but can tolerate higher for long context jobs. Cost is a factor, we want to understand what Dedicated saves vs hosted.
[01:20] Marcus: Cool — so 32k is in the sweet spot for many open LLMs. To hit your latency - cost mix, options are: 1) Hosted with Redwood (fast onboarding) using optimized 32k variants and caching; 2) Dedicated reserved pools — lower per-token cost and predictable capacity; 3) Private on-prem/VPC for compliance but higher ops overhead.
[01:38] Elena: For multilingual: we've had problems with some community weights — Spanish often loses nuance. Any guidance on model fine-tuning vs instruction tuning?
[01:48] Marcus: From our evals, Llama3 base / instruction variants show good multilingual with instruction tuning; Mistral is strong on English but mixed on smaller languages unless fine-tuned. For Spanish+French we usually recommend a small targeted fine-tune or RLHF-like instruction tuning on your domain data. Quantized weights like q4m or q8 can still preserve multilingual but need validation.
[02:10] Samir: On tool-calling, we need deterministic function calling to hit our vector DB and an internal API for user data. How does Redwood support tool calls?
[02:20] Jenna: Redwood supports structured function/tool calling and streaming. Marcus, want to cover runtime?
[02:24] Marcus: Yeah, runtime supports function calls and we surface a function-calling API in the same REST/SDK interface. There are some caveats with KV cache and tool state; for long-running sessions we recommend pinning KV cache and using our routing policies. The transcription may sound weird but basically we maintain KV/ prefix cache to lower recompute.
[02:46] Elena: KV cache — is that preserved across dedicated nodes? We worry about cold-starts.
[02:52] Marcus: Dedicated pools can be configured with warmers and KV cache persistence — reduces cold-starts. Hosted may have slightly more variance, but we also offer burst capacity and pinned model lanes for an account to reduce jitter.
[03:08] Ravi: About context length: you mentioned 32k fine, but what about 128k? We have large docs (30-50k tokens) for legal summarization.
[03:18] Marcus: 128k is supported for some model families and on specific infra profiles — it's more expensive and increases latency. We usually recommend chunking and retrieval-augmented generation for >64k workflows, unless you need single-pass generation. If you need true 128k, we can run benchmarks; there's also quantization and kernel selection tradeoffs — some kernels perform better at long sequences.
[03:40] Elena: Ok — we may start with 32k and evaluate 64k for a POC.
[03:46] Maya (PM): Timeline: we hope to have a POC by mid-Jan, production by Q2 if things look good.
[03:53] Jenna: Sounds reasonable. We'll send the hosted vs dedicated pricing; Dedicated pricing shows significant savings at consistent high-throughput.
[04:02] Samir: Security questions — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and data residency. Can Redwood meet these?
[04:12] Jenna: Yes — we have SOC2 and ISO docs, SAML for SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments. For Hosted we support customer-managed encryption keys via KMS in some regions, and audit logs in Console. I'll attach security pack.
[04:28] Ravi: For PHI-like logs, we'd likely prefer Dedicated or Private. Any notes on egress and data retention?
[04:36] Marcus: Dedicated gives you more isolation and retention controls. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control. Hosted can be configured with retention policies but not suitable if regs require on-prem only. We'll detail retention options in the security doc.
[04:50] Elena: Benchmarking — what samples do you need? We'll share 500 representative prompts including multi-turn chat, long-doc summarization, and retrieval scenarios.
[04:59] Marcus: Great — send those and we'll run them against a few model candidates: Llama3-instruct-32k, Mistral-instruct-32k, and a quantized Llama2-70B-32k variant. We'll provide latency/cost/quality breakdown and token-level traces.
[05:16] Ravi: Any caveats around tool-calling and streaming for function calls? We've seen partial responses and aborted calls in other platforms.
[05:24] Marcus: We stream function arguments and support resume/fallback. For mission-critical transactional calls we recommend ack patterns and idempotency at your API layer. There's also model-specific behavior — sometimes function call formatting varies across model families, so testing is important.
[05:41] Elena: Multilingual fidelity — will you provide evals with native Spanish speakers?
[05:46] Marcus: We can run automated metrics plus a small human eval (native speakers) as part of the POC. We'll include token-level diff and hallucination checks.
[05:55] Jenna: Ok let's recap next steps: Jenna sends pricing & security; Marcus sends benchmark plan and temporary creds; Praxis provides prompt set and target SLOs; then POC kickoff week of 2027-01-09.
[06:08] Ravi: Sounds good. Any competitor concerns? We've also talked to Anthropic and Replicate; want to be sure Redwood's performance and cost stack up.
[06:16] Marcus: We'll include competitor baseline numbers where feasible. One note: model variants and kernel choices can change perf radically — we try to pick realistic baselines.
[06:27] Maya: Can you provide an example rollout plan for Dedicated — like canary -> full, auto fallback to hosted?
[06:34] Jenna: Yes — Redwood supports canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model variants. We'll include a sample rollout doc.
[06:43] Samir: Network-wise, for Dedicated/VPC, do you support strict egress rules and private peering?
[06:48] Marcus: Yes, VPC peering and private connectivity are supported; we'll add network design notes.
[06:55] Elena: Ok, any blockers?
[06:58] Ravi: none from my side, just want the docs and benchmark asap.
[07:02] Jenna: Thanks all — we'll follow up with attachments.

(End of transcript)

Notes: transcription has occasional speaker mislabels; some product names transcribed as 'Redwooddedicated' in audio auto-gen. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/decks/praxis-model-selection.pdf , security pack link (will be sent via email).
